success_criteria.description: All three districts are in use and every precinct is assigned.
All three districts have roughly equal population (within 15%).

character.name: You
character.motivation: Three candidates are on the ballot in the Bend: Sean for the Ken Party out west, Sakura for the Ryu Party in the city, and Dhalsim — the unaffiliated yogi the Hollow reveres — running as an Independent in the east. Three bases, three corners. Where you draw the lines decides how many of them win.

intro_slides.body: The west is Ken country, where Sean runs strong. The city core leans Ryu behind Sakura. And out east, in the Hollow, the Independent Dhalsim takes about half the vote — ahead of both parties on his home ground.
intro_slides.heading: A Three-Cornered Race

intro_slides.body: Each candidate has one part of the Bend. Draw a district around each base — west, city, Hollow — and all three can win a seat. Blur those lines and one base can swallow another, or split Dhalsim's Hollow until his half-here, half-there adds up to nothing.
intro_slides.heading: Three Bases, Three Corners

narrative.objective: Draw three balanced, connected districts — a legal map, like before — and read the result. There's no seat to chase; repaint the lines and watch the three-cornered race change — can you draw a map where Sean, Sakura, and Dhalsim each carry a seat?
narrative.epilogue: A third voice changes the map. An Independent with a concentrated base is powerful when his community stays together and powerless when it's split — the same packing-and-cracking that moves seats between two parties. The lines don't just pick between two sides; they decide whose voice counts at all — and whether three corners can each keep their champion.
